name: Inland (Micro Center)
summary: Private store brand of US electronics retailer Micro Center, with no separate corporate entity, website or social presence. Inland filament is produced by eSUN or Polymaker (project-owner verified), identifiable by the spool cutout: diamond = Polymaker, round = eSUN. The catalogue mirrors those OEMs' own lines at Micro Center's budget in-store pricing.

oem_relationships.notes: User-verified (research/verified-oem-relationships.md): round spool cutout indicates eSUN production. Community mapping (VORON Design forum, not manufacturer-confirmed) matches Inland HS-PLA+ to eSUN PLA+ and notes eSUN spools carry an internal cardboard reinforcing ring; the same thread places this eSUN production in Vietnam.

User-verified (research/verified-oem-relationships.md): diamond spool cutout indicates Polymaker production. Community mapping (VORON Design forum, not manufacturer-confirmed) matches Inland PLA Matte to Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA and Inland Cosplay PLA to Polymaker CosPLA Type A, and notes Polymaker spools have a pill-shaped hole near the spindle.

product_lines.name: PLA
product_lines.notes: Base PLA; Micro Center staff describe it as cheap, low in temperature resistance and relatively brittle.

product_lines.name: PLA+
product_lines.notes: PLA with an impact-toughening agent added. Community-identified as equivalent to eSUN PLA+.

product_lines.name: High Speed PLA+
product_lines.notes: Flow-optimised PLA+, so it carries both the toughened and the high-flow ids.

product_lines.name: Tough PLA
product_lines.notes: Toughened PLA line; impact modifier not itemised.

product_lines.name: Silk PLA (incl. Mystic Silk, Silk Rainbow, Chameleon)
product_lines.notes: Described as 'a PLA polyester composite'; higher print temp 235-245 C, consistent with silk grades generally.

product_lines.name: Matte PLA
product_lines.notes: Community-identified as equivalent to Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA.

product_lines.name: PLA Glitter Rainbow
product_lines.notes: Glitter-particulate PLA; no glitter-PLA id exists in the catalog (see gaps).

product_lines.name: Wood PLA
product_lines.notes: PLA with wood fibre filler.

product_lines.name: PLA Carbon Fiber (PLA Pro / PLA-CF)
product_lines.notes: PLA with chopped carbon fibre.

product_lines.name: Lite PLA (LW-PLA)
product_lines.notes: Lightweight foaming PLA - 'less PLA and more of a plant fiber filler', expands during printing to cut part mass.

product_lines.name: Glass PLA
product_lines.notes: Translucent 'glass-look' PLA. Deliberately NOT mapped to pla-gf: there is no glass-fibre reinforcement, the name refers to optical appearance.

product_lines.name: Cosplay PLA
product_lines.notes: Community-identified as equivalent to Polymaker CosPLA Type A (a low-temperature, easily sandable/heat-formable PLA).

product_lines.name: PETG / PETG+
product_lines.notes: PETG+ is an enhanced shelf-life/printability grade on the same base resin as the standard PETG.

product_lines.name: PETG-CF
product_lines.notes: Carbon-fibre-filled PETG.

product_lines.name: ABS
product_lines.notes: Plain ABS.

product_lines.name: ASA
product_lines.notes: UV-stable ABS alternative.

product_lines.name: PolyLite ASA
product_lines.notes: Same ASA chemistry sold under the licensed 'PolyLite' sub-brand, consistent with the Polymaker OEM relationship.

product_lines.name: PC (Polycarbonate)
product_lines.notes: Plain PC.

product_lines.name: Tough PC
product_lines.notes: Impact-modified PC. Whether the modifier is an ABS blend is not disclosed, so pc-abs is not asserted.

product_lines.name: Nylon (PA)
product_lines.notes: 'Self-lubricating', highly moisture-sensitive; the specific polyamide grade is undisclosed and multiple blends have shipped, so only the generic pa id is asserted.

product_lines.name: Nylon Carbon Fiber (PA-CF)
product_lines.notes: Carbon-fibre-filled nylon of undisclosed polyamide grade. The catalog only has grade-specific CF nylons (pa6-cf, pa12-cf, ppa-cf), none of which can be confidently assigned (see gaps).

product_lines.name: TPU
product_lines.notes: Flexible TPU; Shore hardness not published, so no Shore-grade id is asserted.

product_lines.name: PP (Polypropylene)
product_lines.notes: True polypropylene: described as completely non-bioreactive, low hotend temperature (~160 C), flexible and chemical-resistant.

additional_notes: Inland is a label, not a manufacturer, so manufacturing_countries reflects its OEMs: China for Polymaker-sourced lines and Vietnam for eSUN-sourced lines (the Vietnam detail is community-reported and not manufacturer-confirmed). There is no Inland website, documentation, wiki or social media; the Micro Center category page is the only endpoint. Micro Center stocks build plates and PEI sheets in store but they are Creality-branded, so makes_plates is false. In-store filament typically runs $17-20/kg. Community quality complaints about Inland silk PLA appear on the Bambu Lab forum (anecdotal, unverified). Spools carry no manufacturer information, so consumer-facing sourcing is deliberately opaque.

provenance.conflicts: The verified-oem-relationships file names eSUN generically while the VORON forum thread places eSUN's Inland production in Vietnam specifically; this is treated as a refinement rather than a contradiction, but it is community-sourced and not manufacturer-confirmed. The same thread cautions that sourcing could change at any time and that all SKU-to-OEM mappings are indirect, so per-line OEM assignment should not be considered settled.
